Bryce Canyon, USA

If wind had hands, it would carve something like Bryce. A vast amphitheater of stone spires rises in southern Utah, each hoodoo frozen mid-motion — like figures caught in an eternal dance. These otherworldly formations stand like silent sentinels, each telling a story older than memory.

At sunrise, the canyon comes alive. The first light spills across the rocks, painting them in warm tones of rose, copper, and gold — as though another world is slowly opening its eyes.

Nestled just off Scenic Byway 12 — one of America’s most stunning drives — Bryce Canyon invites exploration.

The ideal time to visit is May through October. Spring awakens the meadows with wildflowers, summer remains cool thanks to the high elevation (over 2,400 m), and fall drapes the landscape in deep, fiery hues. In winter, a soft blanket of snow transforms the hoodoos into a dreamlike, stone-carved fairytale.
